author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Commit only when your estimate beats the price
summary: Do not act on a candidate unless your independent probability estimate exceeds the market or default-priced probability by a defined margin. The size of the edge, not the appeal of the option, licenses action.
usable_principle: EV gate: estimate your true probability, compare to the priced-in probability, act only when the gap clears a set threshold (for example model 60 percent vs priced 51 percent).
sniped_relevance: BASEPLATE pricing and deal selection: only pursue an engagement when expected value beats the cost and the alternative use of the hour. SNIPED: only run a lane when its expected return beats the floor offer.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Profit lives where posted price diverges from true probability
summary: Across any fragmented set of providers or markets, opportunity concentrates where a posted price has drifted from the true odds. The discipline is to hunt the divergence, not to predict the outcome.
usable_principle: Treat inefficiency as the asset. Scan fragmented markets (tools, channels, pricing, attention) for where the going price has not caught up to reality, and act there.
sniped_relevance: BASEPLATE: AI-tool and channel arbitrage (underpriced capability before the market reprices). SNIPED: underpriced-attention channels before they crowd.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Prefer high-volume low-variance over lottery outcomes
summary: Bias every commitment toward outcomes with a high probability of clearing a floor over outcomes with a high ceiling and high variance. Survival and base-rate stability beat upside chasing.
usable_principle: Floor over ceiling: prefer recurring, high-probability, low-variance returns over rare high-multiplier gambles. Optimize to clear the floor first, chase ceiling only with surplus.
sniped_relevance: SNIPED: recurring Reset/retainer revenue over one-shot whales. Content: consistent volume over viral gambles. BASEPLATE: dependable retainers over moonshot bids.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Size positions to the variance of the spot
summary: Set commitment size by the uncertainty of the situation, not by how confident you feel. High uncertainty means a smaller stake or a pass. Use fixed sizing tiers so size is a deliberate choice.
usable_principle: Size to variance, not conviction. Use named stake tiers (anchor, value, speculative, pass) and let the variance of the spot pick the tier. Pass is a first-class option.
sniped_relevance: BASEPLATE: scale deal commitment and capital to how knowable the outcome is. SNIPED: scale spec/free work to how validated the relationship is.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Verify ground truth before forming an opinion
summary: Refuse to act on stale or assumed inputs. Before any judgment, confirm the current facts (date, who is present, what changed). A removed assumption upstream silently breaks a downstream conclusion.
usable_principle: Scan first: verify the live ground truth before forming any opinion, and refuse to reason on stale or assumed inputs.
sniped_relevance: SNIPED pre-shoot verification (confirm location, talent, gear before the shutter). BASEPLATE intake hygiene (confirm scope and constraints before committing).

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: State how it dies before you commit
summary: Require one explicit, observable, numeric kill-condition per option before committing. If you cannot state how the thesis breaks, you do not understand it well enough to act.
usable_principle: Pre-commit a numeric kill-condition for every decision: the specific observable event at which you reverse or exit. No kill-condition, no commitment.
sniped_relevance: Mirrors the OS decision-memo reversibility/kill-criteria. Applies to offers, hires, tools, and campaigns.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
summary: One role generates options each tagged with its failure conditions; a different role selects. Splitting the seats prevents an analysis from grading its own homework and surfaces blind spots.
usable_principle: Separate the analyst seat (generate candidates with explicit failure conditions) from the decider seat (select against the rules). Do not let one seat do both.
sniped_relevance: This OS already uses it (workflow find-then-adversarially-verify). Apply to any high-stakes BASEPLATE or SNIPED call.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
summary: Enumerate the worst-case scenarios, then score each option by the fraction of them it survives. Require a survival threshold (for example 3 of 4) to qualify. Robustness beats peak expected value when ruin is possible.
usable_principle: Run a bad-script survival filter: list the ways it can go wrong, keep only options that survive a set fraction of them.
sniped_relevance: BASEPLATE risk screening for engagements and commitments where a bad outcome is costly. SNIPED: screen lanes that could damage reputation.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: A banned category forces PASS regardless of edge
summary: Evaluate non-negotiable constraints before optimizing. If a candidate falls in a banned category, force a pass no matter how strong the edge looks. Constraints are gates, not penalties.
usable_principle: Check hard constraints first and let them override optimization. A strong edge inside a banned category is still a pass.
sniped_relevance: Maps to the OS Class A hard-constraint taxonomy (the command router refuses Class A regardless of upside).

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Anchor on the reference-class base rate first
summary: Start every estimate from the base rate of the reference class before adjusting for the specific case. Most participants lose; most launches fail. Anchor there, then move only on diagnostic evidence.
usable_principle: Outside view first: anchor on the reference-class base rate, then adjust for case specifics weighted by how diagnostic the evidence is.
sniped_relevance: Pricing, forecasting, and go/no-go decisions across SNIPED and BASEPLATE. Tempers optimism with honesty.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Trust models for synthesis, never for live facts
summary: Large models give strong general strategy and framework synthesis but fail on live ground truth (stale numbers, outdated entities). Use them to reason, never to source current facts, and always reconcile against a controlled source of truth.
usable_principle: Split LLM use: advisor for synthesis and framework, never for live facts. Feed the model structured ground truth you control, then reconcile its output against that source.
sniped_relevance: Directly answers the recurring frustration that ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude/Grok disagree. The fix is reasoning-mode selection plus ground-truth reconciliation, not trusting one model.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Anchor model reasoning to data you supply
summary: Upload structured ground truth (a compiled table, screenshots, a CSV) so the model reasons over facts you control, then persist the whole workflow as a reusable custom tool or project.
usable_principle: Ground-truth ingestion: compile the facts into structured input, have the model reason over them, then save the prompt+structure as a reusable tool.
sniped_relevance: The OS ingestion pipe and the custom-GPT/Gem pattern (see the Kling Gem). Reusable for any decision-support tool.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Output confidence bands, not binary yes/no
summary: Force calibration by outputting tiered confidence bands with an explicit avoid list, rather than a binary call. Tiers make over- and under-confidence visible and auditable.
usable_principle: Output a tiered, calibrated decision (high/medium/low conviction bands) plus a named avoid list, instead of a single yes/no.
sniped_relevance: Mirrors the OS tiered execution-prioritization. Apply to any prioritized action queue or pipeline review.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: An upstream absence creates a downstream opportunity
summary: When a constraint, competitor, or input drops out of a system, a predictable opportunity vacuum opens downstream. Hunt for where demand or usage concentrates when something is removed.
usable_principle: Watch for removed constraints: when a competitor, tool, or team member exits, map where the freed demand or usage predictably flows, and move there.
sniped_relevance: BASEPLATE and SNIPED opportunity scanning: where a competitor's gap or a market exit concentrates winnable demand.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
summary: Reduce every headline price to cash in hand after platform fees, processing, shipping, materials, priced labor, and tax. The sale price is never the profit. Set break-even off the real number.
usable_principle: Compute fully-loaded net per unit: gross minus fees, processing, fulfillment, consumables, your own hourly labor, and tax. Decide off that, not the sticker.
sniped_relevance: SNIPED pricing floor and any side venture: protects the $1,500 floor logic and exposes work that is negative once labor is priced.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Fixed costs punish low tickets, reward a higher floor
summary: Flat and percentage fees combine so that low-ticket transactions are structurally unprofitable and a dead-zone middle band nets worse than expected. Raising the price floor above the dead zone fixes the math.
usable_principle: Map the fee curve: identify the price band where fixed costs eat the margin, and set a floor above it. Low tickets and the mid dead-zone are traps.
sniped_relevance: Reinforces the SNIPED floor discipline with the actual fee math, not just positioning.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Gross catalog value overstates realizable value
summary: A liquidation is not N clean sales. The last fraction of inventory is the hardest to move and drags the realized average well below list, tying up capital at high opportunity cost. Speed and certainty of exit have real value.
usable_principle: Discount for liquidity: assume the long tail does not clear, that the last 20 percent is the hardest, and that a fast certain exit (even at a haircut) can beat a slow full-price grind.
sniped_relevance: Inventory, prints, edition products, and any asset-backed venture. Also frames retainer cash certainty over lumpy project revenue.

author: BJ (operator method, abstracted from personal analytics corpus)
concept: Convert any DIY task to an implied wage
summary: Price your own time at an explicit hourly rate, convert any cost-saving or DIY task into an implied wage, and compare to the value of your time. Outsource and accept a haircut whenever DIY pays below your rate.
usable_principle: Make-vs-delegate by effective hourly wage: if doing it yourself implies a wage below your time's value, delegate and accept the haircut.
sniped_relevance: Directly informs the SNIPED retoucher/assistant delegation decisions and the lean-override hour budget.
